problems.title: Six statistics for a nine-value data set
problems.question: For $1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,5$, find mode, median, mean, range, variance and standard deviation.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: $\bar x=\sum x_i/N$; population variance $=\sum x_i^2/N-\bar x^2$; standard deviation is its square root.
steps: The mode is 3 (three occurrences), and the middle fifth value is 3. The sum is 27 over nine values, so the mean is 3. Range is $5-1=4$.
The square sum is $1+8+27+32+25=93$. Thus variance is $93/9-9=4/3$, and standard deviation is $2/\sqrt3$.
problems.answer: Mode 3; median 3; mean 3; range 4; variance $4/3$; standard deviation $2/\sqrt3$.
problems.note: The school data variance uses division by N. An unbiased sample-variance convention would instead divide the squared-deviation sum by N−1.

problems.title: Two disjoint dice events
problems.question: Two fair independent dice are rolled. $A$ means both odd; $B$ means both even. Find probabilities of $A,A\cap B,A\cup B,A\setminus B$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes; disjoint-event probabilities add.
steps: Three odd choices on each die give 9 outcomes for $A$, so $P(A)=1/4$. Similarly $P(B)=1/4$.
The events are disjoint, so intersection probability is 0, union probability is $1/2$, and $A\setminus B=A$ has probability $1/4$.

problems.title: Complementary, disjoint and independent die events
problems.question: For one fair die, $A=$ even, $B=$ odd, $C=$ prime, $D=$ composite, $E=$ multiple of 3. Classify pairs as complementary, disjoint or independent.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Complements partition the sample space; disjoint pairs have empty intersection; independence means $P(U\cap V)=P(U)P(V)$.
steps: Disjoint pairs are $A,B$; $B,D$; and $C,D$. In particular, 1 is neither prime nor composite, so $C,D$ are not complements.
$P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=1/2$, $P(D)=P(E)=1/3$. Each of $A\cap E,B\cap E,C\cap E$ has one outcome, probability $1/6=(1/2)(1/3)$. All other pair intersections fail the product test.

problems.title: Three independent attempts
problems.question: Three independent shooters hit with probabilities 0.6,0.7,0.8. Find probabilities of all missing, at least one hit, and exactly one hit.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Multiply independent probabilities; add disjoint alternatives; $P(\text{at least one})=1-P(\text{none})$.
steps: All miss: $0.4\cdot0.3\cdot0.2=0.024$. At least one hit: $1-0.024=0.976$.

problems.title: A coin with a different bias on each toss
problems.question: On toss $j$, one face has probability $1/(j+1)$. Show that the other face on toss $n$ has the same probability as at least one first-face result in the first $n$ tosses.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Assuming independent tosses, the probability of no first-face result is $\prod_{j=1}^n j/(j+1)$.
steps: The product telescopes to $1/(n+1)$. Therefore the probability of at least one first-face result is $1-1/(n+1)=n/(n+1)$.
The other face on toss $n$ has probability $1-1/(n+1)=n/(n+1)$ too.
problems.answer: Both probabilities equal $n/(n+1)$ for independent tosses.
problems.note: The calculation needs independence (or the corresponding conditional-probability model). Marginal probabilities alone do not determine the probability of at least one success.

problems.title: A divisibility proof by modular reduction
problems.question: Prove $3^{n+1}5^n+2^{3n+2}$ is divisible by 7 for every natural $n$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Rewrite the expression as $3\cdot15^n+4\cdot8^n$.
Modulo 7 this is $3\cdot1^n+4\cdot1^n=7\equiv0$. Thus divisibility holds for every $n$.

problems.title: Circumcircle of a coordinate right triangle
problems.question: $A=(1,1),B=(9,7),C=(1,7)$. Find the circumcircle equation.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: The circumcenter of a right triangle is the hypotenuse midpoint.
steps: $AC$ is vertical and $CB$ horizontal, so $C$ is the right vertex. The hypotenuse $AB$ has midpoint $(5,4)$.
Its half-length is $\sqrt{8^2+6^2}/2=5$.

problems.title: Intersection, angle and distances for two lines
problems.question: Lines $a:3x-2y=7$, $b:x+2y=13$ and point $A=(1,1)$ are given. Find their intersection $B$, smaller-angle cosine, $AB$, and distance from $A$ to $a$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Add the line equations to get $4x=20$, hence $B=(5,4)$.
Directions $(2,3),(2,-1)$ have dot product 1 and length product $\sqrt{65}$, so the smaller-angle cosine is $1/\sqrt{65}$.
$AB=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5$. The distance from $A$ to $a$ is $|3-2-7|/\sqrt{13}=6/\sqrt{13}$.

problems.title: Perpendicular lines enclosing a prescribed area
problems.question: Find two perpendicular lines through $(0,2)$ that form, with the $x$ axis, a triangle of area 5.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Take slopes $m,-1/m$, with intercepts $-2/m,2m$ on the $x$ axis.
steps: The triangle height is 2 and base length $2|m+1/m|$. Thus area is $2|m+1/m|=5$.
The solutions are $m=2,1/2,-2,-1/2$. After removing duplicate orderings, two line pairs remain.

problems.title: Orthocenter from two perpendicular slopes
problems.question: $A=(2,1),B=(4,7),C=(8,3)$. Find the intersection of the triangle altitudes.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: $BC$ has slope $-1$, so the altitude through $A$ is $y=x-1$. $AB$ has slope 3, so the altitude through $C$ is $y-3=-(x-8)/3$.
Substitute to get $3x-3=17-x$, hence $x=5,y=4$.
